title: Build a single-site VCF migration architecture
prompt:
Create the deployable migration architecture for the estate in `files/estate-inventory.json`. The destination is the single-site consolidated VMware Cloud Foundation design described by that fixture and must remain at its minimum supported host count while honoring its stated failures-to-tolerate.

Before designing, use real network access to research Broadcom-published sources for: the supported migration or upgrade path from every inventoried source version, content/configuration compatibility and exceptions, lifecycle/end-of-support boundaries, and the VCF management-domain host-count/FTT constraint. Record the pages you actually consulted, access date, and the claim each page informed in `research-sources.md`. Use current, reachable Broadcom sources of your choice; do not treat the local compatibility snapshot as a substitute for this research.

Implement the design as `VcfMigrationArchitecture.psd1` and `VcfMigrationArchitecture.psm1`, a PowerShell module whose exported `Export-VcfMigrationPlan` command has mandatory `-InventoryPath`, `-CompatibilityPath`, and `-OutputPath` parameters. Running

`Import-Module ./VcfMigrationArchitecture.psd1`
`Export-VcfMigrationPlan -InventoryPath ./files/estate-inventory.json -CompatibilityPath ./files/compatibility-snapshot.json -OutputPath ./migration-plan.json`

must produce `migration-plan.json` conforming to `files/migration-plan.schema.json`. The JSON is the architecture of record, not prose. It must contain an ordered plan; identify every source product, exact version and support boundary; map each to its target component and exact version; enumerate content/configuration that carries forward and what is abandoned; attach technical gates to each component and step; and include target placement and per-node sizing. Preserve the fixture's IDs verbatim. Resolve researched facts against the pinned `files/compatibility-snapshot.json`, which is the fixed compatibility authority for this deliverable. Do not change anything under `files/`.
